reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended Argument filtering still drops valid empty-object calls and can incorrectly invoke tools with defaults after aggregating empty argument deltas when a stream reaches the length limit.
2 open issues - [Preserve empty argument objects when filtering truncated calls](https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel/pull/14727#discussion_r4482342460) · New - [Track whether streamed tool arguments were actually received](https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel/pull/14727#discussion_r4482342563) · New
What changed in this PR This PR addresses #14723 by filtering unwritten tool calls from Python’s automatic function-calling loops when a response reaches the token limit, preventing unintended execution with default arguments. **Changes:** - Adds shared filtering before history insertion and invocation in streaming and non-streaming paths. - Adds mocked OpenAI connector tests for skipped calls and compatibility cases. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `python/​tests/​unit/​connectors/​ai/​open_ai/​services/​test_openai_chat_completion_truncated_tool_call.py` | Adds six regression tests covering both response paths. | | `python/​semantic_kernel/​connectors/​ai/​chat_completion_client_base.py` | Filters empty-argument calls in length-limited replies and exits when none remain. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: This truthiness check drops completed empty argument objects (`{}`) from connectors such as Google AI and Bedrock when the reply hits the length limit, while retaining the equivalent OpenAI string `'{}'`. Restrict both filtering predicates to `None` or `""` so valid no-parameter/defaulted calls keep their existing behavior.

When two deltas for the same call contain only empty/`None` arguments, `FunctionCallContent.combine_arguments` produces `'{}'`, so this filter still invokes the tool with defaults if the stream ends with `length`. Preserve whether arguments were actually received during aggregation, without rejecting explicitly written `'{}'`, and add a split-delta regression test.
